reason: The study evaluates alcohol consumption in relation to general prostate cancer in a case-control design. It does not report an aggressive, high-grade, advanced, metastatic, or lethal endpoint. A literal total sample size is not stated; cases and controls are reported separately.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: No noteworthy relationship was found for major measures of alcohol intake: compared with teetotallers, the multivariate relative risks (RRs) of prostate cancer, after adjustment for age, study center, education, marital status, body mass index, and smoking status, were 1.3, 0.9, 1.2, and 1.1, respectively, for men drinking fewer than three, three to less than five, five to less than eight, or more than eight alcoholic beverages per day.
estimate_classifications.reason: The row's greater-than-eight-drinks comparison is the final category in this overall prostate cancer analysis and is not restricted to aggressive disease.
